title: How Seasonal Reference Choice Changes the Apparent Gains of Chronos Models in Electricity Load Forecasting
abstract: arXiv:2611.29653v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: When a forecasting model is said to beat a simple baseline, the size of that win depends on which baseline was used. We measure how much this matters for two zero-shot foundation models, Chronos-Bolt and Chronos-2, on hourly electricity load. The study uses 60 fixed cases drawn from eight series in four public collections, with forecasts 24 and 168 hours ahead and up to 2,048 hours of history. Each model is compared with daily persistence, weekly persistence, a weekday hybrid, a daily-weekly blend, and a reference chosen from these on a validation period. We keep every origin-level forecast and estimate uncertainty with paired circular block bootstrap intervals using 168- and 336-hour blocks. A week ahead, Bolt clearly beats weekly persistence in 21 of 30 cases but the validation-selected reference in only 14, and its median gain falls from 17.3% to 11.9%. For Chronos-2 the clear-win counts are 18 and 15. Chronos-2 has lower week-ahead M

translated_title: 季节性参考基线的选择如何改变Chronos模型在电力负荷预测中的表观收益
translated_abstract: 当宣称某个预测模型胜过简单基线时，其胜出的幅度取决于所选用的基线。我们针对两个零样本基础模型——Chronos-Bolt和Chronos-2——在小 时级电力负荷数据上量化了这一问题的重要性。研究使用从四个公开数据集的八条序列中抽取的60个固定案例，预测提前期为24小时和168小时，可用历史数据最多为2,048小时。每个模型分别与日持续性、周持续性、工作日混合模型、日-周混合模型，以及在验证期从中选出的参考基线进行比较。我们保留了每个预测起点的预测结果，并采用基于168小时和336小时块的配对循环块自助法区间来估计不确定性。在提前一周的预测中，Chronos-Bolt在30个案例中的21个明显胜过周持续性基线，但仅在14个案例中明显胜过验证期选出的参考基线，其中位数收益从17.3%降至11.9%。对于Chronos-2，明显胜出的案例数分别为18和15。Chronos-2在提前一周预测方面具有较低的M……
tldr: 研究表明Chronos基础模型在电力负荷预测中的表观优势高度依赖于季节性参考基线的选择：Chronos-Bolt提前一周预测时在30个案例中的21个明显胜过周持续性基线（中位收益17.3%），但换成验证期选出的参考基线后仅剩14个案例明显胜出（中位收益降至11.9%）。
en_tdlr: The study shows that the apparent advantage of Chronos foundation models in electricity load forecasting depends heavily on the seasonal reference baseline chosen: Chronos-Bolt clearly beats weekly persistence in 21 of 30 week-ahead cases (median gain 17.3%), but only 14 against a validation-selected reference (median gain drops to 11.9%).
